Subject: Semantic indexing integration — post-demo recap & next steps

Hi Emma / Devin —

Thanks again for the demo call this morning. Quick recap from our side and proposed next actions so we keep momentum: 

What we heard you need
- High-quality semantic search for product catalog (10M+ items)
- Migration from your current vector store (you mentioned Pinecone) with minimal downtime
- Tight latency SLOs for search queries (~60–120ms p95) and cost visibility
- Ability to run reranking in the request path (reranker model called after 32 nearest vectors)

Key integration considerations we discussed
- Vector dimension preference: you currently store 512-d vectors; we recommended evaluating 768 vs 1024 depending on the new encoder. We should run a quick A/B at two dims.
- Normalization: we discussed L2 normalization versus raw cosine in the index — we'll provide guidance and a sample conversion script.
- Batching: for bulk reindexing of 10M records we recommend 8k–32k item chunks and a background worker using Redwood batching SDK.
- Auth/routing: API keys for initial POC, then OAuth + dedicated routing to your VPC instance for production.

Immediate next steps (proposed)
1) We’ll send a short spec (attached) with recommended vector dims, normalization steps and a sample bulk pipeline.
2) NovaSearch shares a small data sample (~1k records) and an example query set so we can prototype recall/latency tradeoffs.
3) Ben to propose a migration-runbook and downtime profile.
4) Schedule a technical session (45 min) with your infra and our solutions engineering — available Wed/Thu next week.

Attachments: redwood-embed-spec-v1.pdf (embedding guidance + migration checklist)

If that all looks good, I’ll lock in a time for the tech session.

Thanks —
Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Semantic indexing integration — post-demo recap & next steps

Thanks Tessa — this is great and captures the call. A few clarifying points from our side: 

- Dimension: we currently use 512 with a legacy encoder. We plan to evaluate a new encoder that outputs 768. Running an A/B at 512 vs 768 makes sense. We're open to a 1024 experiment but want to understand cost/latency implications first.
- Reranker: yes, reranker will be a lightweight BERT-based model that we can host; we prefer the reranker call to happen synchronously after vector search (we can tolerate ~100ms extra).
- Migration: Pinecone hosts our current indexes. We need a plan that supports incremental reingestion and fallbacks if a few documents fail during conversion.

We attached a small sample export for you: novasearch-sample-1000.csv (ID, title, description, current_vector_512).

Wed/Thu next week looks good — prefer Thu afternoon if possible (PDT).

Best,
Emma
Senior Product Manager, NovaSearch

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Semantic indexing integration — post-demo recap & next steps

Emma — thanks for the sample. Quick technical notes based on an initial pass (Jonas and I will expand these in the tech session):

1) Dimensionality and recall tradeoff- 512 -> smaller disk/ram footprint, faster nearest-neighbor ops; 768 -> generally higher recall for our encoders; 1024 -> diminishing returns unless you include wider context windows. For your catalog I recommend prototype runs at 512 vs 768 first.

2) Normalization- We recommend L2-normalizing vectors prior to indexing when using inner-product libraries that expect normalized inputs (or you can store raw and use cosine at query time). Script in the attached PDF shows batch convert: compute L2 norm and divide.

3) Bulk migration strategy- Incremental approach: (A) Export from Pinecone in chunks (we can help with export script), (B) Normalize & transform to target dim if changing encoder (we provide conversion + rescore examples), (C) Import into Redwood-backed index under a 'shadow' namespace, (D) Run shadow queries for 24–48 hours and compare recall/latency, (E) Switch routing to new namespace and keep fallback to legacy for 7 days. Expect tooling to handle ~5–10k/sec ingest in burst for your instance class; we'll size dedicated capacity during POC.

4) Batching recommendations- For reindex workers use dynamic batching: up to 4k items per batch for CPU workers, up to 32k when GPU-based pre-encoding is available. We'll include SDK snippets for both.

5) Auth & routing- POC: API keys scoped to a single project. Prod: recommend mTLS to your VPC endpoint + workload identity. We'll coordinate keys rotation and route-based policies (dedicated for search queries, lower-cost fallback for batch jobs).

Attachments included: redwood-embed-spec-v1.pdf (contains code snippets, L2 conversion script, batch sizing matrix).

Jonas and I can lead the technical session. Tessa — Thu 2027-08-19 14:00 PDT works for us. 

-Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
